<skill_content name="brainstorming">
# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

---

## Comprehensive Project Summary: Agentic ODI

### 1. What is This Project?

**Agentic ODI** is an experimental project that explores how the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. 

Based on Strategyn's ODI methodology (grounded in a PDF at `knowledge/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick), the project implements the core ODI domain concepts:
- **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)**: Stable human functional goals
- **Universal Job Map**: 8 stages (Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Conclude)
- **Desired Outcomes**: Measurable success metrics in the format `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
- **Opportunity Scoring**: `Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)` — scores >10 indicate underserved market opportunities

The MCP server acts as the "brain" of customer needs, letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes.

**Core README reference**: `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/README.md`
**Domain guardrails**: `/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md`

---

### 2. Directory Structure

The repository has **two parallel layouts** — an established top-level layout and a newer `apps/` + `packages/` refactor:

#### Established Layout (active — used by root `pyproject.toml`, CI, and dev workflow)

```
/home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/
├── core/              # agentic-odi-core — Domain models, services, repositories
├── mcp_server/        # agentic-odi-mcp-server — FastMCP server over HTTP
├── local_server/      # agentic-odi-local-server — FastAPI sidecar for Living Studio
├── cli/               # agentic-odi-cli — Typer-based CLI
├── client/            # agentic-odi-client — Dev launcher
├── connectors/        # agentic-odi-connectors — External MCP integrations
├── studio/            # React + TypeScript + Vite SPA + Tauri 2 desktop
├── website/           # Static GitHub Pages marketing site
├── scripts/           # Dev launcher, binary build, installer scripts
├── tests/             # Cross-package contract tests
├── packaging/         # PyInstaller spec for CLI binary
├── infra/cloudflare/  # Cloudflare Worker config for free-tier deployment
├── docs/              # Architecture, reference, and workflow documentation
├── .agents/           # Superpowers skills + agent instructions
├── .github/           # GitHub Actions workflows
├── pyproject.toml     # Root uv workspace config
├── uv.lock            # Pinned dependencies
├── wrangler.jsonc    # Cloudflare Wrangler config
```

#### Newer Refactored Layout (under `apps/` and `packages/`)

```
apps/
├── cli/               # Same as cli/ but with agentic_odi_cli package + extra modules
├── mcp-server/        # Same as mcp_server/ but with agentic_odi_mcp_server package
├── studio-api/        # Same as local_server/ but with agentic_odi_studio_api package
├── studio/            # Same SPA + Tauri as studio/

packages/
├── core/              # Same as core/ but with agentic_odi_core package + new modules
├── connectors/        # Same as connectors/ but with agentic_odi_connectors + new modules
```

**Key differences in the new layout**:
- Package import names use `agentic_odi_*` prefix (e.g., `agentic_odi_core` instead of `core`)
- The new MCP server is significantly larger: 483 lines vs. 241 lines (adds evidence tools, step/outcome CRUD, etc.)
- The new core package adds `contract.py` (single source of truth for MCP tool surface), `evaluation.py`, `factory.py`, and `schema.py`
- The new connectors package adds `mapping.py` and `rest/connector.py` (REST connector)
- The `local_server` package in the old layout uses `from core import ...` while the new `studio-api` uses `from agentic_odi_core import ...`

The git log shows a commit `9ebb72d refactor: reorganize workspace into apps and packages` indicating this migration is in progress, but the **root `pyproject.toml` and all CI workflows still reference the old top-level directories**.

#### Hidden/Infrastructure Directories
- `.agents/skills/` — 15 vendored Superpowers skills (brainstorming, systematic-debugging, TDD, etc.)
- `.github/workflows/` — 6 CI workflows (CI, release, tauri-release, release-please, e2e-install)
- `.worktrees/` — 21 git worktrees for parallel feature development
- `.superpowers/` — Superpowers skill artifacts
- `.wrangler/` — Cloudflare Wrangler cache
- `.venv/` — Virtual environment

---

### 3. Technology Stack

#### Python Backend
- **Language**: Python 3.10+ (3.10, 3.11, 3.12 tested in CI)
- **Package Management**: `uv` (workspace with pinned `uv.lock`)
- **MCP Framework**: [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) — both server and client
- **Web Framework**: FastAPI + Uvicorn (studio sidecar)
- **CLI Framework**: Typer
- **Data Modeling**: Pydantic (BaseModel, computed_field, validation)
- **LLM Client**: OpenAI (OpenAI-compatible API, used with local Ollama/llama-cpp)
- **HTTP Client**: httpx (for MCP and connector calls)
- **Persistence**: SQLite (event-sourced via append-only IntentStore)
- **Concurrency**: asyncio

#### Frontend
- **Framework**: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite
- **Desktop**: Tauri 2 (Rust-based desktop shell)
- **Testing**: Vitest + React Testing Library + jsdom
- **Linting**: ESLint + TypeScript ESLint
- **Build**: Vite (SPA) + Tauri CLI (desktop bundles)

#### Infrastructure & Deployment
- **Cloudflare Worker**: Free-tier deployment (serves static SPA + tunnels `/api/*` to sidecar)
- **Prefect Horizon**: Hosted MCP endpoint (`agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp`)

#### Dev Tools
- **Linting/Formatting**: Ruff
- **Type Checking**: Mypy (per-package config)
- **Security Scanning**: Bandit
- **Testing**: pytest + pytest-asyncio (strict mode)
- **Code Coverage**: pytest-cov + coverage.py + Codecov (90% threshold)
- **Pre-commit**: pre-commit with Ruff hooks
- **Binary Building**: PyInstaller (CLI binary for Linux/macOS/Windows)
- **Agent Session Tracking**: Entire CLI integration
- **Skills Framework**: Superpowers (15 vendored skills in `.agents/skills/`)

---

### 4. Main Components / Modules

#### Core Domain (`packages/core/` or `core/`)
- **`models.py`** — Pydantic models: `Job`, `Step`, `Outcome`, `CustomerValue`, `BusinessValue`, `CustomerOutcome`, `Evidence`, `ValueMetric`, `Direction`, `BusinessImpactCategory`. Includes `compute_opportunity_score()`.
- **`contract.py`** (new layout only) — Single source of truth for MCP tool surface: `ToolName` enum, `ToolSpec` dataclass, `TOOL_SPECS` dict (29 tools covering jobs, steps, outcomes, customer outcomes, evidence, scoring, schema, capabilities, and framework guidelines).
- **`services.py`** — `ODIService` business-logic layer with full CRUD for all entities, opportunity score computation, and evidence promotion.
- **`repository.py`** — `Repository` Protocol + `InMemoryRepository` implementation.
- **`sqlite_repository.py`** — SQLite-backed repository using event-sourcing via `IntentStore`.
- **`intent_store.py`** — Append-only event store (SQLite, WAL mode) with immutable event log.
- **`factory.py`** — `build_repository()` factory (SQLite by default, in-memory for `:memory:`).
- **`schema.py`** — Canonical JSON schemas for all ODI entities.
- **`evaluation.py`** — Outcome statement format validator.
- **`messages.py`** — ODI framework guidelines, capabilities text, system prompts, and error message helpers.

#### MCP Server (`apps/mcp-server/` or `mcp_server/`)
- **`mcp_server.py`** — FastMCP server with 29 `@mcp.tool`-decorated tools:
  - **Jobs**: `add_job`, `get_jobs`, `get_job`, `update_job`, `delete_job`
  - **Steps (Job Map)**: `add_step`, `get_job_map`, `get_step`, `update_step`, `delete_step`
  - **Desired Outcomes**: `add_outcome`, `get_outcomes`, `get_outcome`, `update_outcome`, `delete_outcome`
  - **Customer Outcomes**: `add_customer_outcome`, `get_customer_outcome`, `list_customer_outcomes`, `update_customer_outcome`, `delete_customer_outcome`
  - **Evidence**: `add_evidence`, `get_evidence`, `list_evidence`, `delete_evidence`, `promote_evidence`
  - **Utilities**: `compute_opportunity`, `evaluate_outcome`, `get_odi_schema`, `get_odi_framework_guidelines`, `get_capabilities`
  - **Prompt**: `odi_assistant_prompt`
  - Runs on HTTP transport at `http://localhost:8000/mcp`

#### Studio API / Sidecar (`apps/studio-api/` or `local_server/`)
- **`app.py`** — FastAPI app factory, CORS config, SPA fallback mounting.
- **`main.py`** — uvicorn entry point (port 8100).
- **`studio/router.py`** — API routes: `/api/config`, `/api/health/mcp`, `/api/health/llm`, `/api/canvas`, `/api/steps`, `/api/outcomes`, `/api/chat`
- **`studio/chat.py`** — Streaming SSE chat with LLM tool-loop (OpenAI-compatible), offline fallback responses.
- **`studio/mcp_data.py`** — MCP hydration (fetches jobs/steps/outcomes via MCP, falls back to seed data).
- **`studio/probes.py`** — Connection probing and LLM health checks.
- **`studio/seed.py`** — Demo/prototype data for the Opportunity Landscape.

#### CLI (`apps/cli/` or `cli/`)
- **`cli.py`** — Typer app entry point with subcommands: `chat`, `version`, `update`, `connectors`, `customer-outcomes`, `score`
- **`backend.py`** — Backend abstraction: `LocalBackend` (SQLite, no server), `MCPBackend` (remote MCP over HTTP)
- **`chat.py`** — Interactive terminal REPL with streaming MCP tool-calling loop
- **`customer_outcomes.py`** — CRUD commands for Customer Outcomes
- **`connectors.py`** — Connector management (add/list/health/ingest/catalog)
- **`render.py`** — Human-readable and JSON output rendering
- **`update.py`**: Auto-update engine (binary download, verify, atomic swap)
- **`profile.py`**: User profile persistence
- **`onboard.py`**: First-run onboarding flow

#### Client (`client/`)
- **`run.py`** — Dev launcher that starts MCP server + Studio sidecar concurrently

#### Connectors (`packages/connectors/` or `connectors/`)
- **`protocol.py`** — `Connector` ABC (health + ingest contract)
- **`factory.py`** — Kind registry (`register_kind`, `build_connector`)
- **`registry.py`** — JSON-backed `ConnectorRegistry`
- **`catalog.py`** — 15 built-in MCP connector presets (Notion, Gong, GitHub, Linear, Exa, Slack, etc.) grouped into 5 capability areas
- **`mcp/connector.py`** — `MCPClientConnector` — MCP client that ingests tools/resources from external MCP servers
- **`rest/connector.py`** (new layout) — REST connector
- **`sink.py`** — In-memory ingest sink
- **`models.py`** — Shared Pydantic models

#### Studio Frontend (`apps/studio/src/` or `studio/src/`)
- **29 TypeScript/TypeScriptX files** across:
  - `components/canvas/` — CanvasTabs, DirectCapture, EvidenceStream, ImpactSim, JobMap, OpportunityLandscape, OutcomeCard
  - `components/chat/` — ChatCopilot
  - `api/` — studioApi.ts (API client), sse.ts (SSE parser)
  - `lib/` — odi.ts (ODI math: opportunity score computation)
  - `state/` — StudioContext.tsx (React context for app state)
  - `bridge/` — desktopBridge.ts (Tauri webview bridge)
  - `test/` — test setup

#### Tests
- **Python**: 40+ test files across all packages plus root-level contract tests (`tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`, `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`) and script tests
- **Frontend**: Vitest unit tests for ODI math, SSE parser, sidecar client
- **Website**: pytest-based tests for design system, OG image generation, README sync, and site structure
- **Tauri**: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo check`

---

### 5. Frontend, Backend, or Both?

**Both.** The project is a full-stack system:

- **Backend (Python)**: MCP server, FastAPI sidecar, CLI — all built on the shared `core` domain package
- **Frontend (React + Tauri)**: The "Living Studio" SPA with a Tauri 2 desktop shell
- **The SPA only talks to the sidecar** (`local_server`) over `/api` — it never calls MCP or the LLM directly (trust boundary enforced by CORS and architecture)

---

### 6. Testing Frameworks

| Layer | Framework | Details |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| Python backend | **pytest** + **pytest-asyncio** | Strict mode, `@pytest.mark.asyncio` required on every async test. Tests are fast (<1s), in-memory, self-contained |
| Python coverage | **pytest-cov** + **coverage.py** + **Codecov** | 90% project coverage required, 1% tolerance. Combines coverage from all 6 packages into one `coverage.xml` |
| Frontend | **Vitest** + **React Testing Library** + **jsdom** | Unit tests for ODI math, SSE parser, transport bridge |
| Tauri/Rust | **cargo test/fmt/clippy** | Rust formatting and linting checks |
| Website | **pytest** | Tests for design system, OG image reproducibility, README sync |
| Security | **Bandit** | `bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src ...` |
| Type checking | **Mypy** | Per-package config, run separately for each package |
| Linting | **Ruff** | `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` |

**Testing isolation rules**:
- Test files live next to their package (`packages/*/tests`, `apps/*/tests`)
- `InMemoryRepository` is used in tests; `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` before import for MCP server tests
- Root `tests/conftest.py` sets `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:`

---

### 7. MCP-Related Files and Configurations

The project is fundamentally MCP-centric:

| File/Location | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` | **Single source of truth** for the MCP tool surface — `ToolName` enum, `ToolSpec` dataclass, `TOOL_SPECS` dict defining all 29 tools with their argument names and required fields |
| `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` | Asserts the live FastMCP registry matches `TOOL_SPECS` (names, argument names, required fields) |
| `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py` | Asserts the CLI local-handler keys are a subset of `TOOL_NAMES` |
| `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py` (and `apps/mcp-server/...` new version) | The FastMCP server itself — registers all 29 tools via `@mcp.tool` and one prompt via `@mcp.prompt` |
| `connectors/src/connectors/mcp/connector.py` (and `packages/connectors/...` new version) | MCP **client** connector that acts as an MCP client to ingest tools/resources from external MCP servers |
| `local_server/src/local_server/studio/mcp_data.py` | MCP hydration in the sidecar — calls MCP tools (`get_jobs`, `get_job_map`, `get_outcomes`) to fetch canvas data |

# Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails

This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.

> **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `knowledge/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.

---

## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails

This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.

### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?

ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.

ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.

---

### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done

- A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
- A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
- **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
- ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.

---

### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes

- **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
- Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
- **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):

  > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`

  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.

- **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.

---

### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)

- All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
  1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
  2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
  3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
  4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
  5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
  6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
  7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
  8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs

- **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
- ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.

---

### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)

- Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
  - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
  - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?

- **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):

  ```
  Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
  ```

- **Interpretation**:
  - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
  - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
  - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.

- **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.

---

### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation

- ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
- Segments can be:
  - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
  - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
  - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value

- **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.

---

### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy

Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:

| Strategy | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
| **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
| **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |

- **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.

---

### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent

These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:

| DO | DON'T |
|---|---|
| Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
| Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
| Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
| Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
| Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
| Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
| Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |

---

## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
- **Language**: Python 3.10+
- **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
- **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
- **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
- **UI / Chat Client**: `streamlit`
- **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
- **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
- **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`

---

## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail

`README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
times.

### When to update

Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:

| Change type | Where to update |
|---|---|
| New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |
| New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | `README.md` **Quick Start → Prerequisites** |
| New way to run the project | `README.md` **Quick Start** and `docs/living-studio.md` |
| New MCP tool or capability | `README.md` **Code Overview** / relevant doc |
| New CLI command or flag | `docs/cli.md` |
| New connector kind | `docs/connectors.md` |
| New workflow or agent instruction | `docs/living-studio.md` |
| Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | `docs/deployment.md` |
| Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
| Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |

### Rules

- ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
- ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
- ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `python -m client.run` as the recommended launch command.

144: class ChatSession:
145:     """A streamed tool-calling conversation against an OpenAI-compatible model."""

147:     def __init__(
148:         self,
149:         config: ChatConfig,
150:         openai_client: Any,
151:         mcp_client: Any,
152:         *,
153:         on_tool: Callable[[str, dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,

156:         self.openai_client = openai_client
157:         self.mcp_client = mcp_client
158:         self.on_tool = on_tool
159:         self.messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
160:         self.tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
161:         self.tool_names: list[str] = []

163:     async def initialize(self) -> None:
164:         """Discover the MCP tools once and expose them to the model."""
165:         tools = await self.mcp_client.list_tools()
166:         self.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
167:         self.tool_names = [tool["function"]["name"] for tool in self.tools]
168: 
169:     def clear(self) -> None:
170:         """Drop the conversation history but keep the system prompt and tools."""
171:         self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
172: 
173:     async def _stream_completion(
174:         self, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None
175:     ) -> tuple[str, dict[int, dict[str, str]]]:
176:         stream: Any = await self.openai_client.chat.completions.create(
177:             model=self.config.model,
178:             messages=self.messages,
179:             tools=self.tools or None,
180:             tool_choice="auto" if self.tools else None,
181:             stream=True,
182:         )
183: 
184:         content_parts: list[str] = []
185:         tool_calls: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}
186: 
187:         async for chunk in stream:
188:             choices = getattr(chunk, "choices", None)
189:             if not choices:
190:                 continue
191:             delta = choices[0].delta
192:             if delta is None:
193:                 continue
194:             content = getattr(delta, "content", None)
195:             if content:
196:                 content_parts.append(content)
197:                 if on_delta is not None:
198:                     on_delta(content)
199:             for tool_call in getattr(delta, "tool_calls", None) or []:
200:                 entry = tool_calls.setdefault(
201:                     tool_call.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""}
202:                 )
203:                 if tool_call.id:
204:                     entry["id"] = tool_call.id
205:                 function = getattr(tool_call, "function", None)

207:                     if function.name:

209:                     if function.arguments:

41:   /connect   Configure LLM provider and MCP server (wizard)
42:   /model <name>  Switch to a different model
43:   /mcp <url>     Reconnect to a different MCP server
44:   /clear     Clear the conversation history
45:   /tools     List the MCP tools available to the assistant
46:   /exit      Quit (also /quit)
47: 
48: Anything else is sent to the ODI assistant."""

51: @dataclass(frozen=True)
52: class ChatConfig:
53:     """Connection settings for an interactive chat session."""
54: 
55:     base_url: str
56:     api_key: str
57:     model: str
58:     mcp_url: str

60:     @classmethod
61:     def from_env(
62:         cls,
63:         *,
64:         base_url: str | None = None,
65:         api_key: str | None = None,
66:         model: str | None = None,

69:         """Resolve settings in priority order: explicit arg > env var > LLM profile > default."""
70:         # Lazy import to avoid circular imports between chat and profile.
71:         from agentic_odi_cli.profile import load_llm_profile  # noqa: PLC0415
72: 
73:         try:
74:             llm_profile = load_llm_profile()
75:         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001

78:         return cls(
79:             base_url=(
80:                 base_url
81:                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL")
82:                 or (llm_profile.base_url if llm_profile else None)
83:                 or DEFAULT_BASE_URL
84:             ),
85:             api_key=(
86:                 api_key
87:                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY")
88:                 or (llm_profile.api_key if llm_profile else None)
89:                 or DEFAULT_API_KEY
90:             ),
91:             model=(
92:                 model
93:                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL")
94:                 or (llm_profile.model if llm_profile else None)
95:                 or DEFAULT_MODEL
96:             ),
97:             mcp_url=(
98:                 mcp_url
99:                 or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL")
100:                 or (llm_profile.mcp_url if llm_profile else None)
101:                 or DEFAULT_MCP_URL
102:             ),

129: def _to_openai_tools(tools: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
130:     """Translate FastMCP tool definitions into OpenAI function schemas."""
131:     return [
132:         {
133:             "type": "function",
134:             "function": {
135:                 "name": tool.name,
136:                 "description": tool.description or "",
137:                 "parameters": tool.input_schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
138:             },
139:         }
140:         for tool in tools
141:     ]

144: def _normalize_tool_calls(entries: dict[int, dict[str, str]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
145:     """Turn the per-index streaming tool-call buffers into OpenAI tool calls."""
146:     return [
147:         {
148:             "id": entry["id"] or f"call_{index}",
149:             "type": "function",
150:             "function": {
151:                 "name": entry["name"],
152:                 "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
153:             },
154:         }
155:         for index, entry in entries.items()
156:     ]

159: def _tool_result_text(result: Any) -> str:
160:     """Extract readable text from an MCP tool result."""
161:     content = getattr(result, "content", None) or []
162:     parts = [getattr(item, "text", None) for item in content]
163:     text = "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)
164:     return text or str(result)

167: def handle_command(
168:     line: str,
169:     session: ChatSessionLike,
170:     *,
171:     on_connect: Callable[[], ChatConfig | None] | None = None,
172:     on_mcp_reconnect: Callable[[str], bool] | None = None,
173: ) -> Literal["exit", "handled"] | tuple[str, str] | None:
174:     """Handle a slash command, or return None when the line is a chat message.
175: 
176:     Returns:
177:         "exit"              — caller should end the session.
178:         "handled"           — command was handled; continue the REPL.
179:         ("reconnect_mcp", url) — caller should reconnect MCP then continue.
180:         None                — not a command; caller should send to the LLM.
181:     """
182:     command = line.strip().lower()
183:     if command in {"/exit", "/quit"}:
184:         return "exit"
185:     if command == "/help":
186:         typer.echo(HELP_TEXT)
187:         return "handled"
188:     if command == "/clear":
189:         session.clear()
190:         typer.echo("Conversation cleared.")
191:         return "handled"
192:     if command == "/tools":
193:         if session.tool_names:
194:             typer.echo("\n".join(session.tool_names))
195:         else:
196:             typer.echo("No tools loaded.")
197:         return "handled"
198:     if command == "/status":
199:         state = session.connection_state
200:         llm_status = "connected" if state.llm_ok else "not connected"
201:         mcp_status = (
202:             f"connected ({state.mcp_tool_count} tools)" if state.mcp_ok else "not connected"
203:         )
204:         typer.echo(f"model  : {session.config.model}  [{llm_status}]")
205:         typer.echo(f"url    : {session.config.base_url}")
206:         typer.echo(f"mcp    : {session.config.mcp_url}  [{mcp_status}]")
207:         return "handled"
208:     if command.startswith("/model"):
209:         parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
210:         if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
211:             typer.echo(f"Current model: {session.config.model}")
212:         else:
213:             new_model = parts[1].strip()
214:             new_config = ChatConfig(
215:                 base_url=session.config.base_url,
216:                 api_key=session.config.api_key,
217:                 model=new_model,
218:                 mcp_url=session.config.mcp_url,
219:             )
220:             session.update_config(new_config)
221:             typer.echo(f"Model set to: {new_model}")
222:         return "handled"
223:     if command.startswith("/mcp"):
224:         parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
225:         if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
226:             typer.echo(f"Current MCP URL: {session.config.mcp_url}")
227:         else:
228:             new_url = parts[1].strip()
229:             if on_mcp_reconnect is not None:
230:                 ok = on_mcp_reconnect(new_url)
231:                 if ok:
232:                     typer.echo(
233:                         f"MCP reconnected: {new_url} ({session.connection_state.mcp_tool_count} tools)"
234:                     )
235:                 else:
236:                     typer.echo(f"Failed to connect to MCP at {new_url}")
237:             else:
238:                 typer.echo("MCP reconnect not available in this context.")
239:         return "handled"
240:     if command == "/connect":
241:         if on_connect is not None:
242:             connected_config = on_connect()
243:             if connected_config is not None:
244:                 typer.echo(f"Connected: {connected_config.model} @ {connected_config.base_url}")
245:         else:
246:             typer.echo("Connect wizard not available in this context.")
247:         return "handled"
248:     if command.startswith("/"):
249:         typer.echo(f"Unknown command: {line}. Type /help for commands.")
250:         return "handled"
251:     return None

254: async def _try_connect_mcp(mcp_url: str) -> tuple[Any, list[Any], str | None]:
255:     """Attempt to connect to the MCP server and list its tools.
256: 
257:     Returns:
258:         (mcp_client, tools, None) on success.
259:         (None, [], error_message) on failure.
260:     """
261:     try:
262:         async with Client(mcp_url) as c:
263:             tools = await c.list_tools()
264:         # Re-create a fresh context manager for the caller to manage lifetime.
265:         return Client(mcp_url), tools, None
266:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
267:         return None, [], str(exc)

270: class ChatSession:
271:     """A streamed tool-calling conversation against an OpenAI-compatible model."""
272: 
273:     def __init__(
274:         self,
275:         config: ChatConfig,
276:         openai_client: Any,
277:         mcp_client: Any,
278:         *,
279:         connection_state: ConnectionState | None = None,
280:         on_tool: Callable[[str, dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
281:     ) -> None:
282:         self.config = config
283:         self.openai_client = openai_client
284:         self.mcp_client = mcp_client
285:         self.connection_state = (
286:             connection_state if connection_state is not None else ConnectionState()
287:         )
288:         self.on_tool = on_tool
289:         self.messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
290:         self.tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
291:         self.tool_names: list[str] = []
292: 
293:     async def initialize(self) -> None:
294:         """Discover the MCP tools once and expose them to the model."""
295:         tools = await self.mcp_client.list_tools()
296:         self.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
297:         self.tool_names = [tool["function"]["name"] for tool in self.tools]
298: 
299:     def clear(self) -> None:
300:         """Drop the conversation history but keep the system prompt and tools."""
301:         self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
302: 
303:     def update_config(self, new_config: ChatConfig) -> None:
304:         """Hot-swap the session config and mark the LLM connection as live."""
305:         self.config = new_config
306:         self.connection_state.llm_ok = True
307: 
308:     async def _stream_completion(
309:         self, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None
310:     ) -> tuple[str, dict[int, dict[str, str]]]:
311:         stream: Any = await self.openai_client.chat.completions.create(
312:             model=self.config.model,
313:             messages=self.messages,
314:             tools=self.tools or None,
315:             tool_choice="auto" if self.tools else None,
316:             stream=True,
317:         )
318: 
319:         content_parts: list[str] = []
320:         tool_calls: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}
321: 
322:         async for chunk in stream:
323:             choices = getattr(chunk, "choices", None)
324:             if not choices:
325:                 continue
326:             delta = choices[0].delta
327:             if delta is None:
328:                 continue
329:             content = getattr(delta, "content", None)
330:             if content:
331:                 content_parts.append(content)
332:                 if on_delta is not None:
333:                     on_delta(content)
334:             for tool_call in getattr(delta, "tool_calls", None) or []:
335:                 entry = tool_calls.setdefault(
336:                     tool_call.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""}
337:                 )
338:                 if tool_call.id:
339:                     entry["id"] = tool_call.id
340:                 function = getattr(tool_call, "function", None)
341:                 if function is not None:
342:                     if function.name:
343:                         entry["name"] = function.name
344:                     if function.arguments:
345:                         entry["arguments"] += function.arguments
346: 
347:         return "".join(content_parts), tool_calls
348: 
349:     async def _call_tool(self, call: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
350:         name = call["function"]["name"]
351:         raw_arguments = call["function"].get("arguments") or "{}"
352:         try:
353:             arguments = json.loads(raw_arguments)
354:         except json.JSONDecodeError:
355:             return f"Error: invalid JSON arguments for {name}: {raw_arguments}"
356:         if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
357:             return f"Error: arguments for {name} must be a JSON object"
358:         if self.on_tool is not None:
359:             self.on_tool(name, arguments)
360:         try:
361:             result = await self.mcp_client.call_tool(name, arguments)
362:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
363:             return f"Error calling {name}: {exc}"
364:         return _tool_result_text(result)
365: 
366:     async def ask(self, text: str, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> str:
367:         """Send a message, execute any tool calls, and return the final text."""
368:         if not self.connection_state.llm_ok:
369:             return "No model connected. Type /connect to set one up."
370: 
371:         checkpoint = len(self.messages)
372:         self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
373:         try:
374:             while True:
375:                 content, tool_calls = await self._stream_completion(on_delta)
376:                 if not tool_calls:
377:                     self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})
378:                     return content
379: 
380:                 normalized = _normalize_tool_calls(tool_calls)
381:                 self.messages.append(
382:                     {"role": "assistant", "content": content or None, "tool_calls": normalized}
383:                 )
384:                 for call in normalized:
385:                     result = await self._call_tool(call)
386:                     self.messages.append(
387:                         {
388:                             "role": "tool",
389:                             "tool_call_id": call["id"],
390:                             "name": call["function"]["name"],
391:                             "content": result,
392:                         }
393:                     )
394:         except Exception:
395:             del self.messages[checkpoint:]
396:             raise
397: 
398: 
399: def _print_tool(name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
400:     rendered = json.dumps(arguments, ensure_ascii=False)
401:     if len(rendered) > 100:
402:         rendered = rendered[:97] + "..."
403:     typer.secho(f"  → {name} {rendered}", fg="bright_black", err=True)
404: 
405: 
406: async def _run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> int:
407:     typer.echo("Agentic ODI · interactive")
408: 
409:     llm: Any | None = None
410:     conn = ConnectionState()
411: 
412:     try:
413:         # --- MCP connection (optional) ---
414:         mcp_client_ctx, tools, mcp_error = await _try_connect_mcp(config.mcp_url)
415:         if mcp_error is None:
416:             conn.mcp_ok = True
417:             conn.mcp_tool_count = len(tools)
418:         else:
419:             conn.error_mcp = mcp_error
420:             typer.secho(
421:                 f"⚠  MCP unavailable ({config.mcp_url}): {mcp_error}",
422:                 fg="yellow",
423:                 err=False,
424:             )
425:             typer.secho(
426:                 "   Starting without MCP tools. Use /mcp to reconnect.",
427:                 fg="yellow",
428:                 err=False,
429:             )
430: 
431:         # --- LLM client (always created; actual reachability found on first use) ---
432:         llm = AsyncOpenAI(
433:             base_url=config.base_url,
434:             api_key=config.api_key,
435:             timeout=60.0,
436:         )
437:         conn.llm_ok = True
438: 
439:         # --- Startup banner ---
440:         mcp_status = f"✓ {conn.mcp_tool_count} tools" if conn.mcp_ok else "✗ offline"
441:         typer.echo(f"model: {config.model}  ·  mcp: {config.mcp_url} [{mcp_status}]")
442:         typer.echo("Type /help for commands, /exit to quit.\n")
443: 
444:         # --- Build session ---
445:         session = ChatSession(
446:             config,
447:             llm,
448:             mcp_client_ctx,  # may be None if MCP is offline
449:             connection_state=conn,
450:             on_tool=_print_tool,
451:         )
452: 
453:         # Populate tools from the probe we already did (avoids a second round-trip).
454:         if conn.mcp_ok and tools:
455:             session.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
456:             session.tool_names = [t["function"]["name"] for t in session.tools]
457: 
458:         # --- REPL ---
459:         while True:
460:             try:
461:                 line = input("you › ").strip()
462:             except EOFError:
463:                 typer.echo()
464:                 break
465:             except KeyboardInterrupt:
466:                 typer.echo("\nUse /exit to quit.")
467:                 continue
468: 
469:             if not line:
470:                 continue
471: 
472:             def _on_connect() -> ChatConfig | None:
473:                 from agentic_odi_cli.wizard import run_connect_wizard  # noqa: PLC0415
474: 
475:                 new_config = run_connect_wizard(session.config)
476:                 if new_config is not None:
477:                     session.update_config(new_config)
478:                 return new_config
479: 
480:             def _on_mcp_reconnect(new_url: str) -> bool:
481:                 """Run MCP reconnect in a separate thread (avoids nested event loops)."""
482:                 import concurrent.futures  # noqa: PLC0415
483: 
484:                 async def _reconnect() -> bool:
485:                     _, new_tools, err = await _try_connect_mcp(new_url)
486:                     if err is not None:
487:                         return False
488:                     new_config = ChatConfig(
489:                         base_url=session.config.base_url,
490:                         api_key=session.config.api_key,
491:                         model=session.config.model,
492:                         mcp_url=new_url,
493:                     )
494:                     session.update_config(new_config)
495:                     session.mcp_client = Client(new_url)
496:                     session.tools = _to_openai_tools(new_tools)
497:                     session.tool_names = [t["function"]["name"] for t in session.tools]
498:                     session.connection_state.mcp_ok = True
499:                     session.connection_state.mcp_tool_count = len(new_tools)
500:                     return True
501: 
502:                 with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as executor:
503:                     future = executor.submit(asyncio.run, _reconnect())
504:                     return future.result()
505: 
506:             action = handle_command(
507:                 line, session, on_connect=_on_connect, on_mcp_reconnect=_on_mcp_reconnect
508:             )
509:             if action == "exit":
510:                 break
511:             if action == "handled":
512:                 continue
513: 
514:             typer.secho("odi › ", fg="green", bold=True, nl=False)
515:             printed = False
516: 
517:             def on_delta(piece: str) -> None:
518:                 nonlocal printed
519:                 printed = True
520:                 typer.echo(piece, nl=False)
521: 
522:             try:
523:                 reply = await session.ask(line, on_delta=on_delta)
524:             except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
525:                 typer.echo()
526:                 typer.echo(f"Error: {exc}", err=True)
527:                 continue
528:             typer.echo()
529:             if not printed:
530:                 typer.echo(reply if reply else "(no response)")
531: 
532:     finally:
533:         if llm is not None:
534:             await llm.close()
535: 
536:     typer.echo("Goodbye.")
537:     return 0
538: 
539: 
540: def run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> None:
541:     """Run the interactive chat until the user exits."""
542:     try:
543:         exit_code = asyncio.run(_run_chat(config))
544:     except KeyboardInterrupt:
545:         typer.echo("\nGoodbye.")
546:         return
547:     if exit_code:
548:         raise typer.Exit(code=exit_code)

1: """Backend abstraction for the CLI.
2: 
3: Two backends implement the same :class:`Backend` seam:
4: 
5: * :class:`LocalBackend` runs the ODI logic directly against a local SQLite
6:   store (no server required).
7: * :class:`MCPBackend` delegates to a remote MCP server over HTTP, which may be
8:   a local ``python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`` process or a hosted endpoint.
9: 
10: Commands resolve a backend once from the options stored on
11: :mod:`agentic_odi_cli.context`. Keeping the local and remote paths behind one interface
12: means the same command works against either, and a future hosted backend only
13: has to implement ``call``.
14: """

548:     stripped = text.strip()

2:  * Headline copy for the conversational home screen.
3:  *
4:  * The hero line is the only "chrome" above the composer, so it has to earn its
5:  * space: it greets when it knows who you are, reflects what is already on the
6:  * canvas when there is data, and otherwise explains what the studio can do.
7:  * The lines rotate so the surface feels alive rather than static.
8:  */
9: 
10: export interface GreetingContext {
11:   now: Date;
12:   displayName?: string | null;
13:   jobCount: number;
14:   outcomeCount: number;
15:   underservedCount: number;
16:   llmHealthy?: boolean | null;
17: }
18: 
19: export type GreetingKind = "greeting" | "insight" | "capability" | "status";
20: 
21: export interface Greeting {
22:   id: string;
23:   text: string;
24:   kind: GreetingKind;
25: }
26: 
27: /** Seconds between hero rotations. Exported so the UI and tests agree. */
28: export const GREETING_ROTATION_MS = 7000;
29: 
30: function cleanName(displayName?: string | null): string | null {
31:   const trimmed = displayName?.trim();
32:   if (!trimmed) {
33:     return null;
34:   }
35:   return trimmed.replace(/\s+/g, " ");
36: }
37: 
38: export function timeOfDayGreeting(now: Date): string {
39:   const hour = now.getHours();
40:   if (hour >= 5 && hour < 12) {
41:     return "Good morning";
42:   }
43:   if (hour >= 12 && hour < 18) {
44:     return "Good afternoon";
45:   }
46:   return "Good evening";
47: }
48: 
49: function plural(count: number, one: string, many = `${one}s`): string {
50:   return `${count} ${count === 1 ? one : many}`;
51: }
52: 
53: export function greetingCandidates(context: GreetingContext): Greeting[] {
54:   const name = cleanName(context.displayName);
55:   const greeting = timeOfDayGreeting(context.now);
56:   const candidates: Greeting[] = [
57:     {
58:       id: "greeting",
59:       text: name ? `${greeting}, ${name}` : greeting,
60:       kind: "greeting",
61:     },
62:   ];
63: 
64:   if (context.outcomeCount > 0) {
65:     candidates.push({
66:       id: "insight-outcomes",
67:       text:
68:         context.underservedCount > 0
69:           ? `${plural(context.outcomeCount, "outcome")} mapped — ${context.underservedCount} underserved.`
70:           : `${plural(context.outcomeCount, "outcome")} mapped. Nothing is starving for attention.`,
71:       kind: "insight",
72:     });
73:   }
74: 
75:   if (context.jobCount > 0) {
76:     candidates.push({
77:       id: "insight-jobs",
78:       text:
79:         context.jobCount === 1
80:           ? "One job on the canvas. Want to break it into steps?"
81:           : `${plural(context.jobCount, "job")} on the canvas. Want to break one into steps?`,
82:       kind: "insight",
83:     });
84:   }
85: 
86:   candidates.push(
87:     {
88:       id: "capability-job",
89:       text: "What job should we get done today?",
90:       kind: "capability",
91:     },
92:     {
93:       id: "capability-friction",
94:       text: "Tell me where your customers get stuck.",
95:       kind: "capability",
96:     },
97:     {
98:       id: "capability-outcomes",
99:       text: "I turn complaints into measurable outcomes — then find the underserved ones.",
100:       kind: "capability",
101:     },
102:   );
103: 
104:   if (context.llmHealthy === false) {
105:     candidates.push({
106:       id: "status-offline",
107:       text: "No model reachable right now. I can still walk you through the ODI playbook.",
108:       kind: "status",
109:     });
110:   }
111: 
112:   return candidates;
113: }
114: 
115: /**
116:  * Pick the next headline in the rotation, never repeating the current one.
117:  */
118: export function nextGreeting(candidates: Greeting[], currentId?: string | null): Greeting | null {
119:   if (!candidates.length) {
120:     return null;
121:   }
122:   const currentIndex = candidates.findIndex((candidate) => candidate.id === currentId);
123:   return candidates[(currentIndex + 1) % candidates.length];
124: }

1: """Connection probing and LLM health checks, ported from the Streamlit app."""
2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import asyncio
6: import os
7: import socket
8: from urllib.parse import urlparse
9: 
10: from openai import AsyncOpenAI
11: 
12: DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
13: DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
14: DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
15: DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"
16: 
17: OFFLINE_MESSAGE = "LLM server offline (Local Studio Mode enabled)"
18: 
19: 
20: def defaults() -> dict[str, str]:
21:     """Streamlit-compatible environment defaults (same variable names)."""
22:     return {
23:         "base_url": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL", DEFAULT_BASE_URL),
24:         "api_key": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY", DEFAULT_API_KEY),
25:         "model_name": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL),
26:         "mcp_url": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL", DEFAULT_MCP_URL),
27:     }
28: 
29: 
30: def is_endpoint_reachable(url: str, timeout: float = 0.3) -> bool:
31:     """Quick socket check to verify a port is open without hanging on HTTP reads."""
32:     try:
33:         parsed = urlparse(url)
34:         host = parsed.hostname or "localhost"
35:         port = parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme == "https" else 80)
36:         with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=timeout):
37:             return True
38:     except OSError:
39:         return False
40: 
41: 
42: def classify_llm_error(exc: Exception) -> tuple[str, str]:
43:     message = str(exc)
44:     lower = message.lower()
45:     connection_indicators = [
46:         "connection error",
47:         "connection aborted",
48:         "failed to establish a new connection",
49:         "timed out",
50:         "timeout",
51:         "connection refused",
52:     ]
53:     if any(indicator in lower for indicator in connection_indicators):
54:         return "connection_error", message
55:     return "error", message
56: 
57: 
58: async def check_llm_health(base_url: str, api_key: str, model_name: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
59:     """Non-blocking LLM health probe with an instant socket pre-check."""
60:     if not is_endpoint_reachable(base_url, timeout=0.3):
61:         return False, OFFLINE_MESSAGE
62: 
63:     client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key, timeout=1.2)
64:     try:
65:         await asyncio.wait_for(client.models.list(), timeout=1.2)
66:         return True, "LLM backend is reachable."

1: """MCP client connector that ingests tools and resources from an external server."""
2:

12: from fastmcp.client.transports import StreamableHttpTransport
13:

15:     HealthStatus,
16:     IngestBatch,
17:     IngestRecord,

20: from connectors.protocol import Connector
21: 
22: _ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")
23: 
24: 
25: class MissingEnvironmentError(RuntimeError):
26:     """Raised when a connector needs credentials that are not in the environment."""
27: 
28:     def __init__(self, names: list[str]) -> None:
29:         self.names = names
30:         super().__init__("Missing environment variable(s): " + ", ".join(names))
31: 
32: 
33: def _expand_env(value: str, environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
34:     return _ENV_VAR_PATTERN.sub(lambda match: environ.get(match.group(1), ""), value)
35: 
36: 
37: def _to_dict(obj: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
38:     if hasattr(obj, "model_dump"):
39:         dumped = obj.model_dump(mode="json")
40:         if isinstance(dumped, dict):
41:             return dumped
42:     return {"repr": repr(obj)}
43: 
44: 
45: def _content_text(obj: Any) -> str:
46:     parts: list[str] = []
47:     content = getattr(obj, "content", None)
48:     if content is None:
49:         text = getattr(obj, "text", None)
50:         return text if isinstance(text, str) else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
51:     for item in content:
52:         text = getattr(item, "text", None)
53:         if isinstance(text, str):
54:             parts.append(text)
55:     return "\n".join(parts) if parts else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
56: 
57: 
58: class MCPClientConnector(Connector):
59:     """Pulls catalog, resources, and optional tool results from an MCP server."""
60: 
61:     kind = "mcp"
62: 
63:     def __init__(
64:         self,
65:         name: str,
66:         settings: McpConnectorSettings,
67:         *,
68:         server: FastMCP | None = None,
69:     ) -> None:
70:         self.name = name
71:         self.settings = settings
72:         self._server = server
73: 
74:     def transport(self) -> StreamableHttpTransport | FastMCP:
75:         """Build the MCP transport, resolving credentials from the environment."""
76:         if self._server is not None:
77:             return self._server
78:         missing = sorted(name for name in self.settings.env_vars if not os.environ.get(name))
79:         if missing:
80:             raise MissingEnvironmentError(missing)
81:         headers = {
82:             key: _expand_env(value, os.environ) for key, value in self.settings.headers.items()
83:         }
84:         return StreamableHttpTransport(
85:             url=_expand_env(self.settings.url, os.environ),
86:             headers=headers or None,
87:             auth="oauth" if self.settings.auth == "oauth" else None,
88:         )
89: 
90:     def _client(self) -> Client:
91:         return Client(self.transport())
92: 
93:     async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:
94:         try:
95:             async with self._client() as client:
96:                 tools = await client.list_tools()
97:                 resources = await client.list_resources()
98:             return HealthStatus(
99:                 ok=True,
100:                 message="reachable",
101:                 details={
102:                     "tool_count": len(tools),
103:                     "resource_count": len(resources),
104:                 },
105:             )
106:         except MissingEnvironmentError as exc:
107:             return HealthStatus(
108:                 ok=False,
109:                 message=str(exc),
110:                 details={"missing_env": exc.names},
111:             )
112:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
113:             return HealthStatus(ok=False, message=str(exc))
114: 
115:     async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
116:         batch = IngestBatch(connector_name=self.name)
117:         try:
118:             async with self._client() as client:
119:                 tools = await client.list_tools()
120:                 resources = await client.list_resources()
121:                 tool_dicts = [_to_dict(tool) for tool in tools]
122:                 resource_dicts = [_to_dict(resource) for resource in resources]
123:                 catalog_raw = {"tools": tool_dicts, "resources": resource_dicts}
124:                 batch.records.append(
125:                     IngestRecord(
126:                         source_name=self.name,
127:                         source_kind=self.kind,
128:                         item_type="catalog",
129:                         name="mcp-catalog",
130:                         content=json.dumps(catalog_raw, indent=2),
131:                         raw=catalog_raw,
132:                     )
133:                 )
134:                 for resource in resources:
135:                     uri = str(getattr(resource, "uri", ""))
136:                     name = str(getattr(resource, "name", None) or uri)
137:                     try:
138:                         contents = await client.read_resource(uri)
139:                         content_text = "\n".join(
140:                             getattr(item, "text", "") or "" for item in contents
141:                         )
142:                         batch.records.append(
143:                             IngestRecord(
144:                                 source_name=self.name,
145:                                 source_kind=self.kind,
146:                                 item_type="resource",
147:                                 name=name,
148:                                 content=content_text,
149:                                 raw={"uri": uri, "resource": _to_dict(resource)},
150:                             )
151:                         )
152:                     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
153:                         batch.errors.append(f"Failed to read resource {uri}: {exc}")
154:                 configured_tools = self.settings.tools
155:                 available = {str(getattr(tool, "name", "")) for tool in tools}
156:                 for tool_name in configured_tools:
157:                     if tool_name not in available:
158:                         batch.errors.append(f"Tool not found: {tool_name}")
159:                         continue
160:                     try:
161:                         result = await client.call_tool(tool_name, {})
162:                         batch.records.append(
163:                             IngestRecord(

165:                                 source_kind=self.kind,
166:                                 item_type="tool_result",
167:                                 name=tool_name,

169:                                 raw={"tool": tool_name, "result": _to_dict(result)},
170:                             )
171:                         )
172:                     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
173:                         batch.errors.append(f"Failed to call tool {tool_name}: {exc}")

4: against whichever backend is selected (local SQLite by default, or a remote MCP
5: server via ``--backend mcp``).
6: """

9:

12: from typing import Any
13: 
14: import typer
15: 
16: from agentic_odi_cli.backend import run_tool
17: from agentic_odi_cli.render import (
18:     render_customer_outcome,
19:     render_customer_outcome_list,
20:     render_deleted,
21:     render_saved,
22:     render_score,
23: )
24: 
25: customer_outcomes_app = typer.Typer(help="Manage Customer Outcomes.")
26: 
27: 
28: class DirectionOption(str, Enum):
29:     MINIMIZE = "minimize"
30:     MAXIMIZE = "maximize"
31: 
32: 
33: class CategoryOption(str, Enum):
34:     REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
35:     COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
36:     RETENTION = "retention"
37:     RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
38:     OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
39:     COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
40:     BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
41:     OTHER = "other"
42: 
43: 
44: JSON_OPTION = typer.Option(False, "--json", help="Emit machine-readable JSON.")
45: 
46: 
47: def _parse_value_metrics(values: list[str] | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]] | None:
48:     """Parse repeated ``--value-metric`` JSON objects into value metrics."""
49:     if not values:
50:         return None
51:     metrics: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
52:     for raw in values:
53:         try:
54:             parsed = json.loads(raw)
55:         except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
56:             raise typer.BadParameter("must be valid JSON", param_hint="--value-metric") from exc
57:         if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
58:             raise typer.BadParameter("must be a JSON object", param_hint="--value-metric")
59:         metrics.append(parsed)
60:     return metrics
61:

63: @customer_outcomes_app.command("add")

74:     contextual_clarifier: str | None = typer.Option(default=None),
75:     step_id: str | None = typer.Option(default=None),

78:     ),

85:         "object_of_control": object_of_control,

88:         "satisfaction": satisfaction,
89:     }
90:     if contextual_clarifier:
91:         customer_value["contextual_clarifier"] = contextual_clarifier
92:     metrics = _parse_value_metrics(value_metric)
93:     if metrics is not None:
94:         customer_value["value_metrics"] = metrics
95:     args: dict[str, Any] = {
96:         "job_id": job_id,
97:         "customer_value": customer_value,
98:         "business_value": {"category": category.value, "statement": business_statement},
99:     }
100:     if step_id:

158:     if direction is not None:
159:         args["direction"] = direction.value

162:     if object_of_control is not None:

166:     if statement is not None:

171:         args["business_statement"] = business_statement
172:     if detail is not None:
173:         args["detail"] = detail
174:     if estimated_annual_value is not None:
175:         args["estimated_annual_value"] = estimated_annual_value
176:     if confidence is not None:

1: """Rendering helpers: human-readable by default, JSON on request.
2: 
3: Every renderer takes ``as_json`` so the same command can serve a person at a
4: terminal and a script piping into ``jq`` without a second code path.
5: """
6: 
7: from __future__ import annotations
8: 
9: import json
10: from typing import Any
11: 
12: _STATEMENT_WIDTH = 60
13: 
14: 
15: def _json(payload: Any) -> str:
16:     if isinstance(payload, str):
17:         try:
18:             payload = json.loads(payload)
19:         except json.JSONDecodeError:
20:             return payload
21:     return json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
22: 
23: 
24: def _truncate(text: str, width: int = _STATEMENT_WIDTH) -> str:
25:     return text if len(text) <= width else text[: width - 1] + "…"
26: 
27: 
28: def _num(value: Any) -> str:
29:     """Render numeric scores to two decimals; pass anything else through."""
30:     if isinstance(value, bool):
31:         return str(value)
32:     if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
33:         return f"{value:.2f}"
34:     return str(value)
35: 
36: 
37: def _block(rows: list[tuple[str, Any]]) -> str:
38:     """Render label/value pairs as an aligned block."""
39:     width = max(len(label) for label, _ in rows)
40:     return "\n".join(f"{label.ljust(width)}  {value}" for label, value in rows)
41: 
42: 
43: def _table(headers: tuple[str, ...], rows: list[tuple[str, ...]], *, empty: str) -> str:
44:     """Render rows under headers, or ``empty`` when there is nothing to show."""
45:     if not rows:
46:         return empty
47:     widths = [max(len(headers[i]), *(len(row[i]) for row in rows)) for i in range(len(headers))]
48:     lines = ["  ".join(headers[i].ljust(widths[i]) for i in range(len(headers)))]
49:     lines.append("  ".join("-" * widths[i] for i in range(len(headers))))
50:     lines.extend("  ".join(row[i].ljust(widths[i]) for i in range(len(headers))) for row in rows)
51:     return "\n".join(lines)
52: 
53: 
54: def render_job(job: Any, *, as_json: bool) -> str:
55:     """Render one Job as a labelled block or JSON."""
56:     if not isinstance(job, dict):
57:         return _json(job) if as_json else str(job)
58:     if as_json:
59:         return _json(job)
60:     return _block(
61:         [
62:             ("id", job.get("id", "")),
63:             ("name", job.get("name", "")),
64:             ("description", job.get("description") or ""),
65:         ]
66:     )
67: 
68: 
69: def render_job_list(jobs: Any, *, as_json: bool) -> str:
70:     """Render a Job list as an aligned table or JSON."""
71:     if not isinstance(jobs, list):
72:         return _json(jobs) if as_json else str(jobs)
73:     if as_json:
74:         return _json(jobs)
75:     return _table(
76:         ("id", "name", "description"),
77:         [
78:             (
79:                 str(job.get("id", "")),
80:                 _truncate(str(job.get("name", ""))),
81:                 _truncate(str(job.get("description") or "")),
82:             )
83:             for job in jobs
84:         ],
85:         empty="No jobs found.",
86:     )
87: 
88: 
89: def render_customer_outcome(outcome: Any, *, as_json: bool) -> str:
90:     """Render one Customer Outcome as a labelled block or JSON."""
91:     if not isinstance(outcome, dict):
92:         return _json(outcome) if as_json else str(outcome)
93:     if as_json:
94:         return _json(outcome)
95: 
96:     customer = outcome.get("customer_value", {})
97:     business = outcome.get("business_value", {})
98:     rows = [
99:         ("id", outcome.get("id", "")),
100:         ("job_id", outcome.get("job_id", "")),
101:         ("statement", customer.get("statement", "")),
102:         ("direction", customer.get("direction", "")),
103:         ("unit", customer.get("unit_of_measure", "")),
104:         ("object", customer.get("object_of_control", "")),
105:         ("importance", _num(customer.get("importance", ""))),
106:         ("satisfaction", _num(customer.get("satisfaction", ""))),
107:         (
108:             "opportunity",
109:             _num(outcome.get("opportunity_score", customer.get("opportunity_score", ""))),
110:         ),
111:         ("category", business.get("category", "")),
112:         ("business", business.get("statement", "")),
113:     ]
114:     width = max(len(label) for label, _ in rows)
115:     return "\n".join(f"{label.ljust(width)}  {value}" for label, value in rows)
116: 
117: 
118: def render_customer_outcome_list(outcomes: Any, *, as_json: bool) -> str:
119:     """Render a Customer Outcome list as an aligned table or JSON."""
120:     if not isinstance(outcomes, list):
121:         return _json(outcomes) if as_json else str(outcomes)
122:     if as_json:
123:         return _json(outcomes)
124:     if not outcomes:
125:         return "No customer outcomes found."
126: 
127:     headers = ("id", "statement", "importance", "satisfaction", "opportunity")
128:     rows = [
129:         (
130:             str(item.get("id", "")),
131:             _truncate(str(item.get("customer_value", {}).get("statement", ""))),
132:             _num(item.get("customer_value", {}).get("importance", "")),
133:             _num(item.get("customer_value", {}).get("satisfaction", "")),
134:             _num(item.get("opportunity_score", "")),
135:         )
136:         for item in outcomes
137:     ]
138:     widths = [max(len(headers[i]), *(len(row[i]) for row in rows)) for i in range(len(headers))]
139:     lines = ["  ".join(headers[i].ljust(widths[i]) for i in range(len(headers)))]
140:     lines.append("  ".join("-" * widths[i] for i in range(len(headers))))
141:     lines.extend("  ".join(row[i].ljust(widths[i]) for i in range(len(headers))) for row in rows)
